extracted.intended_audience: small businesses, startups, and technology-focused entrepreneurs seeking SBIR/STTR funding
extracted.subtask_description: High-level informational guidance about the SBIR and STTR programs: who they serve, how they are administered, available support, and key program limits and requirements for award administration. Useful for entrepreneurs and support organizations preparing to pursue SBIR/STTR awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity-free / non-dilutive funding
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR provides equity free funding through federal agencies to American small businesses. America’s Seed Fund awards non-dilutive funding to develop your technology and chart a path toward commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that SBIR/STTR awards do not take equity and are intended as non-dilutive capital for technology development and commercialization activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target recipients — American small businesses and technology-focused entrepreneurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Who We Are: America’s Seed Fund provides technology-focused entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses with funding to develop their ideas and a pathway to commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is aimed at U.S.-based small businesses/startups engaged in R&D and technology development; prospective applicants should be small business entities focused on technology/commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose — support technology development and commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the SBIR and STTR programs, America’s Seed Fund awards non-dilutive funding to develop your technology and chart a path toward commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose projects that advance technology development and have a path toward commercialization; commercialization is an explicit program objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and coordination by SBA and participating federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: America's Seed Fund is coordinated by the Small Business Administration and funded through 11 participating federal agencies that fund innovations through the SBIR/STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA coordinates the overall program while individual agencies provide funding—expect both centralized guidance and agency-specific implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating agencies select and fund qualified proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating agencies' SBIR/STTR programs select and fund qualified proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each federal agency runs its own SBIR/STTR solicitations and selections; applicants must follow the solicitation and selection processes of the agency they target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-level administration within Congressional guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating federal agency administers its own SBIR/STTR program within guidelines established by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While agencies have discretion, they must operate within statutory and Policy Directive limits—applicants should consult both agency solicitations and program policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award size limits without SBA approval (Phase I & II)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of October 2024, agencies may issue a Phase I award (including modifications) up to $323,090 and a Phase II award (including modifications) up to $2,153,927 without seeking SBA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any award above those levels will require a waiver; agencies considering exercising higher authority should review SBIR/STTR Policy Directive §7(i)(4). Applicants should budget and plan projects with these typical award ceilings in mind and check current Policy Directive/agency guidance for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver requirement for awards above statutory/administrative thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any award above the stated Phase I/Phase II levels will require a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and agencies must follow SBA Policy Directive procedures (see §7(i)(4)) when requests or awards exceed stated thresholds; higher-than-usual awards are exceptional and require additional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA roles — oversight, policy, and support
rubrics_metrics.description: As the sponsoring agency for America's Seed Fund, SBA guides the participating agency's implementation of their SBIR/STTR programs, monitors and reports on program progress to Congress, and aggregates agency solicitation information. SBA's expert staff supports the program by administering the Policy Directive and liaising with participating federal agencies and technology entrepreneurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA is the central policy and oversight authority—applicants can rely on SBA for high-level policy, aggregated resources, and program monitoring; for specifics follow agency solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support ecosystem and available assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerators, technical assistance centers, and other support organizations around the country help startups identify and apply for awards. "Find Local Assistance" and agency/awards data and success stories are provided as resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to use local accelerators and assistance centers for proposal preparation and commercialization support; the site points to success stories, annual reports, and award data as practical resources.
